meta.title: Seven Details That Tell the Story of a Place
meta.excerpt: A doorway, a patch of shade, a repaired wall: seven everyday clues that reveal how a place is lived in, not merely looked at.
meta.headerQuote: A place rarely tells its whole story through its monuments.
meta.author: Sree Jith
meta.alt: Landscape travel photograph introducing the everyday details of a lived-in place.

cover.alt: Landscape travel photograph introducing the everyday details of a lived-in place.

slides.title: Begin at the Doorway
slides.text: A worn doorstep, shoes set aside, a curtain lifted for air. Thresholds show where private routines meet the life of the street.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on doorways and the boundary between home and street.

slides.title: Notice Where Shade Falls
slides.text: A verandah or tree canopy is more than shelter. Watch who gathers there, and you begin to understand a place’s daily rhythm.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on shade as shared public space.

slides.title: Read the Walls Closely
slides.text: Laterite, limewash, timber, fresh cement: materials carry histories of climate, available skills, changing budgets, and the choice to repair rather than replace.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on buildings, materials, and traces of repair.

slides.title: Look at What Is in Season
slides.text: Market stalls offer a changing map of nearby farms, waters, and kitchens. What arrives in abundance often says more than a souvenir shelf.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on seasonal produce and daily markets.

slides.title: Follow the Water
slides.text: Wells, steps, canals, rain channels: water shapes where people build, gather, grow food, and find relief. Its route is part of the settlement’s design.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on water sources and settlement design.

slides.title: See What Gets Repaired
slides.text: A stitched bag or mended chair reveals useful knowledge. Repair tells us what a community values enough to keep in circulation.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on the everyday work of maintenance and repair.

slides.title: Stay for the Ordinary Hour
slides.text: After the landmark crowds leave, a street keeps speaking through greetings, games, and evening errands. Observe gently; people are not exhibits.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on unhurried everyday encounters in public spaces.
